cases.question: Which button swings the sword?
cases.answer: The A button swings the sword.

cases.question: How much does the Blue Candle cost?
cases.answer: The Blue Candle costs 60 Rupees in the shop described in the 1st Quest overworld walkthrough, and also 60 Rupees in the 2nd Quest shop in Hyrule section 8.

cases.question: How many Heart Containers do I need to get the White Sword?
cases.answer: You need five Heart Containers to receive the White Sword, according to the Items document. The Hyrule 3 cave entry also says at least 5 Heart Containers are needed. One overworld walkthrough says six heart containers are required, which conflicts with the other sources.

cases.question: Which item can I find in Level-3 of the first quest?
cases.answer: In Level 3 of the first quest, you can find the Raft (chunk zelda1:underworld-quest-1-dungeon-3:001 describes finding it down the stairwell after the compass room). The objectives also list Manhandla, a Heart Container, and the third Triforce piece.

cases.question: How powerful is the Magic Sword?
cases.answer: The Magic Sword has Damage 4 and is four times as powerful as the wooden sword, making it the most powerful sword in the game.

cases.question: How can I sail across the sea?
cases.answer: According to the Raft item, Link can cross lakes and oceans with the raft, but it can only be used at a Dock, and neither of the 'double docks' triggers raft use.

cases.question: Is there somewhere my hearts get refilled without paying?
cases.answer: Yes. Fairies fill Link's hearts: a fairy drop fills 3 hearts, and in the fairy ponds the fairy fills all of your heart meters.

cases.question: How can I win cash by gambling?
cases.answer: In the Money Making Game, which is reached by walking into a tree in Hyrule 1 section D-2 ("Walk inside the tree to play the Money Making Game"). Another entrance is a cave reached by bombing the cliff wall left of center in Hyrule 2 section A-5, and Hyrule 6 section C-5 leads to it by bombing the middle of the north wall.

cases.question: What can I buy at D-4 in section 2 of the overworld?
cases.answer: In section 2 of the overworld (Hyrule 2, 2nd Quest), D-4 is a shop where you can buy Arrows for 80 rupees, the Magical Shield for 130 rupees, and a set of 4 Bombs for 20 rupees.

cases.question: What happens if I register my name as ZELDA?
cases.answer: Entering your name as "Zelda" at the start of the game immediately begins the Second Quest without playing the First Quest. The documents do not say whether the name is case-sensitive, so it is unconfirmed that "ZELDA" in all capitals triggers the same result.

cases.question: Where can I buy the Blue Candle, and what can it be used for?
cases.answer: You can buy the Blue Candle for 60 Rupees in a shop reached from the Fairy Fountain by walking three screens south, two screens west, then one screen west and through a door (per the 1st Quest overworld guide). It throws a flame that can light dark dungeon rooms, burn bushes in the overworld, damage enemies, and burn trees for a heart container, though it can only be used once per screen.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Level-1 in the first quest and how do I defeat him?
cases.answer: The boss of Level 1 in the first quest is Aquamentus. You must strike him in the head six times with the Wooden Sword or three times with the White Sword, timing strikes between the energy orbs he emits from his horn. Only the Magical Shield absorbs the orbs, and firing sword beams lets you hit any part of his body.

cases.question: What do I need to enter Level-4 in the first quest, and which item is inside?
cases.answer: To enter Level-4 in the first quest, you need a Raft. The documents list the dungeon's objectives as obtaining the Ladder, a Heart Container, and the fourth Piece of Triforce, but they do not state which single item is found inside.

cases.question: How do I beat the dragon boss?
cases.answer: The dragon boss Aquamentus has 6 HP and shoots fireballs that split in three directions, which can only be blocked by the Magical Shield. It is vulnerable to the Sword and Arrows, and can also be killed by two Bombs.

cases.question: How do I defeat Gleeok?
cases.answer: Each Gleeok head must be stabbed until it flies freely around the room, and the free head is still a threat and cannot be defeated. The only way to beat Gleeok is to destroy every one of its attached heads. Defeating the boss earns a Heart Container.

cases.question: How can I attack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword. Press the B button to use your selected subweapon, such as the Magical Wand.

cases.question: Which button do i have to press to attack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword, which is the attack. The B button is used for subweapons.

cases.question: How can I atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword; press the B button to use your selected subweapon. The Magical Wand also fires magical blasts.

cases.question: how do i open the menu
cases.answer: Press the Start button on controller 1 to bring up the sub-screen menu, where Link can look at the map and change subweapon. Press Start again to return from the sub-screen to the normal view.

cases.question: can i blow up walls with bombz?
cases.answer: Yes. The bomb item documentation says bombs can be used to blast holes in weak walls, and the walkthroughs describe bombing walls to reveal hidden passages.

cases.question: how do i use my secondary item
cases.answer: Your secondary item (subweapon) is used with the B button. To choose which subweapon is assigned to B, open the sub-screen with Start, then use the D-pad to select it.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword. You can also press the B button to use your selected subweapon.

cases.question: how can i heal?
cases.answer: You can heal at the Fairy Fountain, which fully refills your hearts. Fairies found as enemy drops restore 3 hearts. Items like a Water of Life completely refill your life bar, and a Red Potion or Blue Potion from the medicine woman can also be bought in Hyrule 7 (Red Potion 68 Rupees, Water of Life 40 Rupees).

cases.question: where do i find money?
cases.answer: Several places in the documents give money: the Money Making Game is in a cave reached by bombing the rock face immediately left of the start screen (zelda1:cheats:004). In the 2nd Quest, the Money Making Game is inside a tree at Hyrule 1 D-2 (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-1:003), and a man playing it is reached by blowing the whistle at Hyrule 8 A-3 (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-8:002). Red Moblins also give 30 Rupees in a cave behind the wall right of the crack at Hyrule 8 B-4 (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-8:001), and a secret cave at Hyrule 1 B-3 gives 30 Rupees in the 2nd Quest (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-1:003).

cases.question: what is the best weapon?
cases.answer: The most powerful sword in the game is the Magic Sword, which deals 4 damage and is four times as powerful as the Wooden Sword. Link must have twelve Heart Containers before he can receive it.

cases.question: how do i open a locked door?
cases.answer: One cheat reported for the first dungeon is to enter it, immediately leave, and come back, after which the locked door will open. Otherwise, keys open one door each, and Link can carry up to nine until he obtains the magic key.

cases.question: what do i do if ig im stuck
cases.answer: Bomb every wall that does not contain a door, since this typically reveals passageways deeper into the dungeon. Passages to the "eyes" or unmarked rooms on the dungeon map are also often found this way.

cases.question: how do i defeat the dragon?
cases.answer: The dragon is Gleeok, a multi-headed dragon: Link must attack each head, and when a head takes enough damage it detaches and flies around the room, so dodge its projectiles and keep attacking the attached heads until every head is disconnected. The flying heads cannot be hurt, so focus on the heads still attached to the body.

cases.question: where do i get bombs?
cases.answer: In Quest 1, fight and defeat the Moblins in the nearby area until they drop Bombs you can collect; the Fairy Fountain can serve as your headquarters. Quest 2's overworld list also says to get Bombs, but gives no location for them. Dungeon 6 of Quest 1 also offers replacement Bombs, reached by heading one screen north and two screens east from the Water of Life woman.

cases.question: how do i unlock the bow?
cases.answer: In Quest 1, Dungeon 1, the Bow is in room O-1, which has Traps in each corner and a stairwell in the center surrounded by blocks. Push the left-most block aside to enter the stairwell, where you'll find the Bow. You'll need to purchase Arrows to use it, unless you already bought them before finding it.

cases.question: how do i save my game?
cases.answer: To save your game, choose "SAVE" on the Game Over screen using Select and then press Start; this stores your accomplishments until you next play. Alternatively, you can quickly access the Save Screen from the sub-screen menu by pressing Up on the D-pad and A simultaneously on controller 2.

cases.question: how do i get more hearts?
cases.answer: Heart Containers add a permanent heart to Link's life meter; some are found by pushing a tombstone in the Graveyard (Quest 2), burning a tree on Lake Hylia's coast (fourth Heart Container, Quest 1), or bombing a rock at the foot of the eastern mountains (sixth Heart Container). Fairies fill 3 hearts, and fairy ponds fill all heart meters.

cases.question: can i buy a better shield?
cases.answer: Yes. A Magical Shield is sold in several shops; for example, one in Quest 1 costs 90 Rupees after burning a tree on the way (found by walking north from the green forest), and a shop in the 2nd Quest Hyrule overworld sells one for 130 Rupees in D-4 or 160 Rupees in C-3. A Magical Shield reflects more attacks than the Small Shield you start with.

cases.question: how do i see in dark rooms?
cases.answer: Use a candle to light dark rooms: the Blue Candle works once per screen, and the Red Candle has no per-screen limit. Candles can light up dark rooms in dungeons.

cases.question: Which button do I press to jump?
cases.answer: Press the A button to jump in the air. Jump height is fixed, so tapping or holding A gives the same height.

cases.question: How many spirit points does the windmill star cost?
cases.answer: The windmill star costs 5 spirit points to throw.

cases.question: How many lives does Ryu start with?
cases.answer: Ryu starts the game with two lives in reserve.

cases.question: What happens if the clock runs out before I finish a stage?
cases.answer: You lose one life if the timer runs out before you complete a stage.

cases.question: How can I get higher using just one wall?
cases.answer: Use the wall hop technique: jump toward and cling to a wall, hold the jump button, push away from the wall, then immediately push back toward it. If done correctly you rise and cling to the wall higher than where you started, and repeating this can take you to the top of the screen.

cases.question: Who attacks me in Stage 2-3?
cases.answer: In Stage 2-3, you are first attacked by the enemy known as Bomberhead as soon as you enter the hall.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Stage 3-3?
cases.answer: The boss of Stage 3-3 (Act III) is Basaquer, who leaps back and forth across the room and shoots trios of darts.

cases.question: What does the fire wheel do and does it use spirit points?
cases.answer: The Fire Wheel surrounds Ryu with a circle of fire that eliminates any enemy that contacts him, and it lasts about five seconds before disappearing. It requires no spirit points to use, but it replaces any secondary weapon you currently hold.

cases.question: What is Ninja Gaiden called in Europe?
cases.answer: In Europe, Ninja Gaiden is known as Shadow Warriors.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press B to attack by swinging your sword, and you can attack low by squatting when you attack. Hold Up on the D-pad while pressing B to use your secondary weapon, which requires enough spirit points.

cases.question: how do i get more ninpo?
cases.answer: The documents do not clearly explain how to get more Ninpo (ninja techniques); they mention collecting techniques in lamps and candles and that spirit points are needed to use secondary weapons, but do not describe a Ninpo supply or refill method. Spirit points can be gained from blue tiles (5 points) and red tiles (10 points).

cases.question: how do i heal?
cases.answer: The documents mention health-restoring potions that you can collect: in Stage 4-2, a lamp on the left gives a potion that restores some lost health; in Stage 3-1, a health-restoring potion lies over a small dock segment; in Stage 2-2, an insect item holds a health-restoring potion; and in Stage 5-2, a candle above the first potion contains a health-restoring potion. Collecting these items is how the documents describe healing.

cases.question: why did i get sent back to 6-1?
cases.answer: The documents say that if you lose to any of the final bosses in Stage 6-3's door section, you are returned all the way to 6-1, regardless of how many lives you have left. Defeated bosses stay dead, but a health refill is given only once before each boss. Losing to Jaquio after coming directly from the previous boss battle, with no spirit power, is also described, and defeating the Masked Devil and then dying sends you back to 6-1 to face Jaquio with spirit power.
